There is one vertical resistor between A and B. A is also connected to the upper inner node C through one diagonal resistor, and connected to the rightmost node R through one resistor on the outer upper diagonal branch. B is connected to the lower inner node D through one diagonal resistor, and connected to the rightmost node R through one resistor on the outer lower diagonal branch. There is one vertical resistor between C and D. C and D are respectively connected through resistors to the middle-right node E, and E is then connected through one horizontal resistor to R. All resistors are 1 Ω. This circuit is mirror-symmetric about the horizontal central axis: A and B correspond, C and D correspond, and E and R lie on the axis of symmetry. Reasoning: According to the specified method, let the port be applied with symmetric voltages A = +V/2, B = -V/2. Since the circuit is mirror-symmetric under the exchange A↔B, C↔D, the nodes E and R located on the axis of symmetry are virtual grounds. The midpoints of the resistors A-B and C-D crossing the symmetry plane are also virtual grounds, so each 1 Ω resistor is equivalent in the half-circuit to 1/2 Ω to ground. Analyze only the upper half-circuit. From A to virtual ground there are three types of parallel branches: first, the upper half of the A-B resistor, with resistance 1/2 Ω; second, the outer upper branch resistor from A to R, because R is virtual ground, so it is 1 Ω; third, A first goes through the 1 Ω resistor A-C to C, and then from C to virtual ground. From C to virtual ground there are two parallel paths: the upper half of the C-D resistor 1/2 Ω, and the 1 Ω resistor from C to E, so the equivalent resistance from C to ground is (1/2 || 1) = 1/3 Ω. Therefore the total resistance of the third branch is 1 + 1/3 = 4/3 Ω. Therefore the equivalent resistance of the upper half-circuit is R_half = (1/2 || 1 || 4/3).
